Maya (docs): Heads-up — opened a docs PR to relabel 'rate slab' -> 'usage tier' on the billing dashboard and add a tiny SDK migration snippet for header changes. Need a quick review today if possible. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/6421 :eyes:
Tom (billing): Link 404 for me, CI didn't build?
Jae (devex): Works for me. Maya, can you paste the critical snippet here so I can sanity-check the API examples?
Maya (docs): Sure — pasted below (Python + JS examples):
```python
# python example: include meter header for new usage metric
import requests
headers = {"x-rw-meter": "inference_unit"}
resp = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/generate", headers=headers, json={"prompt": "hi"})
```
```js
// node example using fetch
await fetch(url, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers: { 'x-rw-meter': 'inference_unit' },
  body: JSON.stringify({ prompt: 'hi' })
});
```
Sam (infra): Quick note: backend meter is named `inference_unit` (singular) — let's explicitly show how teams map old token counts to IU for billing. Eg: `iu = ceil(tokens / 128)` (we bill per-128-token unit).
Tom (billing): Good call. Also need to clarify burst-credit semantics — customers keep seeing "spikes consumed burst credits" on the dashboard and asking if that counts as quota.
Jae (devex): For dashboard panel, I updated the example query to use meter_name = 'inference_unit' and group by `usage_tier` dimension. Draft query (pseudo-SQL):
```
SELECT usage_tier, SUM(consumed) AS total_iu
FROM billing_usage
WHERE meter_name = 'inference_unit'
  AND ts >= $__from AND ts <= $__to
GROUP BY usage_tier
ORDER BY total_iu DESC
```
Maya (docs): Added a short migration note explaining token->IU mapping and called out the dashboard panel change. Also fixed an internal broken link that pointed to /metering/billing-metrics (was missing a trailing slash).
DocsBot: Preview build succeeded — staging: https://deploy.preview.redwood.company/docs/billing/usage-tiers :sparkles:
Tom (billing): LGTM except one small nit: can we spell out that burst credits are consumed before quota and do not change per-second rate_limit behavior? Customers interpret "burst" as bigger per-second allowance.
Sam (infra): Added two lines in the PR: "Burst credits are applied to cumulative allowance and can absorb short spikes. They do not increase the configured per-second rate limit; if RPS exceeds the rate window the request will be throttled even if burst credits remain."
Maya (docs): Pushed those edits. Anyone object to backporting the explanatory note to v1.9 (enterprise docs)?
Jae (devex): No objection — low-risk clarifying docs.
Tom (billing): :thumbsup: merging after CI turns green.
DocsBot: Merge completed — PR #6421 merged into main, deploy started.
Maya (docs): Thanks all, will follow up with a short changelog entry and a support blurb for CS.
Tom (billing): Please ping me before the CS blurb goes live so I can confirm billing wording.
Maya (docs): Will do — thanks!
